what_it_does: Multimodal AI models process both text and images (or video), and generating their output one token (word-piece) at a time is inherently sequential and slow. Speculative decoding is a technique where a smaller, faster draft model proposes several tokens ahead of time and a larger, more accurate target model verifies them in parallel — tokens that pass verification are accepted, giving a speedup without changing the final output. Adapting speculative decoding to multimodal models is tricky because the draft and target models are harder to align when both images and text are involved. AASD addresses this by reusing the target model's stored intermediate results (called key-value pairs — the model's running record of what it has seen so far) to help the draft model produce better guesses. A learned compression module keeps those stored results compact, and a special attention mechanism (the step where the model weighs how much each past token matters for the current one) is designed to keep the draft and target models closely synchronized.
